name: unified_log
description: Read a unified log archive with Apple's `log show --archive` (on macOS) or Mandiant's unifiedlog_iterator (elsewhere; a copy of /private/var/db, diagnostics and uuidtext side by side, is staged as one archive first: bounded by max_stage_files and max_stage_bytes, refusing a link, a special file or a member in both trees with different bytes, and removed afterwards). Every decoded entry is kept as a file in out_dir (the reader's own output, stderr and its sha256); entries is a preview of `limit`. The output is read once, in a stream, so the counts cover all of it: lines, JSON records, entry records, lines that are not JSON records, and JSON records with none of an entry's fields (counted apart, not as entries). status is about the run, not the archive, and is one of failed (a reader that exited 0 and wrote no file counts), partial (a reader that exited non-zero, overran its time or was stopped by a signal, lines that did not parse, or an output with no entries, which reader_outcome calls empty; what was written is kept) or complete, with status_basis saying what it rests on; complete is not a coverage claim: decoded_coverage.support_files is a census of the tracev3, timesync, uuidtext and dsc files the input holds, and whether they cover the interval asked about is for the examiner. The reader's version and path are recorded. predicate, start and end are Apple log only; unifiedlog_iterator keeps the full JSONL for downstream queries. Apple's log evaluates the predicate over the messages as it decodes them, not over the text this answer prints: a predicate that names the text of a message (eventMessage, composedMessage, formatString) makes entry_count a count of matches that a preview with withheld text does not show, and a count tells a true guess of a withheld piece from a wrong one. The answer warns whenever a predicate is used, and a job run as secret output refuses a predicate that names message text (predicate_names_message_text); a predicate on process, subsystem, category, sender or time is the way to select there (those fields are evidence text too, and a predicate on a withheld process path is not blind). out_dir must not already hold an earlier run's output. The timeout (timeout_seconds, clamped to 1100) is one budget for staging, the census and the reader: the reader is given what is left of it (budget in the answer says how it was spent), a reader that overruns that leaves a partial receipt, and the counting of its output follows with 70 seconds of its own at most and the sha256 of the output is given up 85 seconds after the budget (a count that was cut says at which line, a sha256 that was not computed is null and a problem; the manifest allows 1200 seconds). SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end the reader this tool started and the processes it started (the reader's descendants, followed from its pid; nothing is searched by name), remove the staged copy, count what the reader wrote for at most 5 seconds and answer once with status partial, interrupted set to the signal's name and exit 128 plus the signal. A reader that overruns the budget is ended the same way. A stop signal that arrives while the answer is being sealed (up to 10 seconds, with a large preview) waits for the answer and is named in it: interrupted is set, status is partial and the exit code is 128 plus the signal. A signal that arrives while the text of the answer is being made or written (a few tenths of a second for an answer of 20 to 44 MB) cannot be put into a text that is already out: it is found afterwards, the exit code is still 128 plus the signal and stderr says that the answer on stdout is whole and was not marked (before this, 2 of 18 signals sent in that window to knowledgec_query and 2 of 14 to fsevents_parse ended with exit code 0 and an answer that said complete). SIGKILL cannot be handled. SIGKILL leaves the staged copy (.logarchive-input in out_dir, up to 16 GiB; out_dir is then refused as already used, so remove it or use another). The preview shows an entry under both readers' field names (time, message, raw_message, pid, thread_id, event_type, log_type as well as Apple's); a record that is an entry by a key whose value is empty is previewed by its key names, not as the whole row. A reader that exits 0 but wrote to its error stream gets a warning. A directory under the staged trees that cannot be read stops the staging (a tree with a part left out is not the evidence), and one under a .logarchive that cannot be read is counted in decoded_coverage.support_files.directories_unreadable and warned. SENSITIVE: log messages can carry command lines, paths, account and host names and the occasional secret. The reader's whole output, which output names, holds every message as the reader decoded it and is not judged by the boundary: it is a file of the job, so run the tool as a job with secret_output: true when messages may hold a secret. WITHHOLDING: the preview (entries) and every other string of the answer are judged by a boundary (with a check of the tool's own around it). The windows-forensics pack's shared boundary block, copied byte for byte (a test holds the copies equal), judges every key and value of the answer and of an error answer, by the type of the field it fills: a name, path, key or URL is shown as it is only when it fits a plain grammar (a path component by component; GUIDs, SIDs, addresses, 0x numbers, times and hexadecimal ids up to 24 digits are plain); free text has token-shaped runs, user-info, the value after a secret's name, vendor-prefixed tokens, padded base64 and PEM keys withheld; and a second check, written apart from the first, reads it all once more, the text as the evidence wrote it as well as the text shown (a string it replaces makes a complete answer partial and is listed under boundary.replaced_at). A withheld text is <withheld N characters: reason>. Past the judging time (10 seconds for an answer or a row, and never past the seal stop of the tool) the strings the evidence supplied are no longer judged: each is replaced whole and the answer is partial, except the names this tool wrote itself and a string of 15 characters or fewer made only of letters, digits, _ and . that does not start like a vendor token. Measured on random plants in a message, a process path, a subsystem, a category, a library path and the key name of a record (rates, not guarantees; a second measurement planted 1,000 per shape and slot with both readers' spellings, and tests/pack-macos-forensics-boundary.test.ts plants 300 per shape and asserts the bounds). Of the 21 shapes the boundary claims (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, SendGrid, Google and npm tokens, AWS key ids, JWT, PEM private keys, user-info with an @ in the password, Password= and password: values, NUL and zero-width splits, base64 keys of 16, 20 and 32 bytes, AWS-shaped keys of 40 characters, random base62 of 24 and 40 characters) 18 were printed whole in 0 of 1,000 plants in every slot; base64 keys of 16 bytes as a process path in 56 of 1,000 (Apple's names) and 42 of 1,000 (Mandiant's) and 16 of 1,000 as a sender path (a / in the key splits it into pieces under 16 characters), of 20 bytes in 9 of 1,000 as a process path and 8 of 1,000 as a library path, and random base62 of 24 characters in 1 of 1,000; a piece of 12 characters of an AWS-shaped key was printed in 2 of 1,000 plants and of a base64 key of 32 bytes in 2. This tool prints no field as hexadecimal, so the cut-token case of the other two tools does not arise here. A FileVault recovery key was printed in 30 to 47% of plants (a message 31%, a process path 47%); after a rule of its own, which looks for the six groups wherever they stand, also next to other letters or digits, 0 of 100 as a message and as a process path. The shapes it does not claim are printed: a plain password, a four-word passphrase and a UUID-shaped key, 1,000 of 1,000; a BitLocker recovery key (eight groups of six digits), 1,000 of 1,000; a random token of 16 characters with spaces or - _ . among them (a Wi-Fi password) in 35 to 67% of plants; random base62 of 16 characters in 0.4 to 1.0%, of 20 in 0.1 to 0.9%, of 32 in 0.1 to 0.2%; text written as spaced characters, as HTML entities, as hexadecimal with spaces or as percent escapes in a text field, 1,000 of 1,000. A path under /var/folders is shown with the alias of the user's temporary folder id in place of an id the block would withhold (as in fsevents_parse): the same id is the same alias in every run and in every tool. The key names of a record that has no entry fields are ordered under the clock of the count. NOT recognised, by design: a secret that does not look like one (a plain password or passphrase, a pronounceable passphrase, a UUID-shaped key, a hexadecimal secret of up to 24 digits in a name, random bytes with no text in them, anything under 16 characters in a name): withholding is by shape, so a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true. A cost: sudo's PWD= field is taken for a password's name and its value is withheld. This tool writes no values file: the originals are in the reader's output.

path.description: A .logarchive, or a directory holding diagnostics and uuidtext (staged for unifiedlog_iterator only)

predicate.description: Apple log only: an NSPredicate, e.g. 'process == "sudo"'. It is evaluated by log over the messages as decoded, so a predicate on message text makes entry_count a count a withheld preview does not show: the answer warns, and a job run as secret output refuses it

start.description: Apple log only: start time, e.g. '2026-02-14 00:00:00'; give an offset, the reader's zone is not this tool's to say

out_dir.description: A new directory for the reader's own output, under work/<your id>/ (as a job it is $OUT/<name>: a job writes only under $OUT, and an out_dir elsewhere is refused with the reason). It is refused if it already holds a file of this tool's from an earlier run

limit.description: Entries previewed inline (default 500); every entry is in the output file

timeout_seconds.description: One budget, in seconds, for staging, the census and the reader (default 900, at most 1100: a larger value is clamped and the answer says so); the reader gets what is left, and what it wrote is kept and counted

max_stage_files.description: Staging a diagnostics and uuidtext copy is refused over this many files (default 1000000); nothing is staged

max_stage_bytes.description: Staging is refused over this many bytes (default 17179869184); nothing is staged
